elements.element: Customer pays no liquidated damages or penalties.
elements.evidence: Revised § 13.5 retains the deeming language: "Customer acknowledges that the Termination for Convenience Fee is a reasonable approximation of such damages and shall be deemed to be liquidated damages and not a penalty", and § 11.1 still obliges Customer to pay that fee. A Customer-payable liquidated amount therefore survives; the drafter correctly does not claim the preferred level.

elements.element: Any Customer-payable liquidated amount is only an early-termination fee.
elements.evidence: Op 3 deletes the separate "Termination for Cause Fee" and substitutes the § 11.1 fee, so § 11.2(A) now reads "Customer shall pay M&I the Termination for Convenience Fee determined and payable as set forth in Section 11.1 above"; § 11.1 characterises that amount as "an early termination fee". § 13.5 as revised deems only that one fee liquidated damages. The retained reimbursements (unamortized Conversion costs, reasonable Expenses) are actual-cost reimbursements, not liquidated amounts, and § 9.2(D) credits run in Customer's favour.

elements.element: The early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Op 1 replaces the REDACTED percentage of "Estimated Remaining Value" with a fixed "amount equal to three (3) times the average monthly Fees payable by Customer during the three (3) months prior to the Effective Date of Termination" — exactly three months of fees, not exceeding the fallback threshold; because § 11.2(A) now points to the § 11.1 amount, the same quantum bounds the default-triggered fee.

elements.element: The early-termination fee is the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer.
elements.evidence: Op 4 adds to § 13.5: "The Termination for Convenience Fee is the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer under this Agreement." This is unconditional, stated once, and consistent with the deletion of the Termination for Cause Fee; no other Customer-payable liquidated formula, instalment or contingent penalty mechanic remains (the § 11.1 50/50 payment timing merely schedules the single capped fee).

reasons: Fallback checklist is position-complete: a single early-termination fee, fixed at three months' average Fees, expressly declared the sole Customer-payable liquidated amount in operative text rather than only in the comment.

Preferred is unreachable on this drafting because § 13.5 still deems the fee liquidated damages payable by Customer; the finding correctly targets the fallback and notes the shortfall rather than claiming it.

Minimality holds: edits are confined to the quantum of the § 11.1 fee, the retirement of the duplicate Termination for Cause Fee, and one exclusivity sentence. Favourable existing language is retained (Expenses wording verbatim, one-year notice, § 11.3 carve-out, § 11.2(B) no-fee treatment of an M&I default), and no survival tail, at-own-expense language, extra damages category or unrelated boilerplate was added. Deleting "Customer or " from the § 11.1 scoping sentence (op 2) is a necessary conforming repair, not a new term: without it the retained sentence would contradict revised § 11.2(A), which now charges the same fee on a Customer-default termination.

Intent preserved: § 13.5's reference to "Sections 11.1 or 11.2(A)" remains accurate; the exclusivity statement is enacted only once (no duplicated tail in § 11.2(A)); the § 13.4 carve-out survives only for the surviving fee, so no dangling cross-reference results; and "Estimated Remaining Value" (Definition N) is left intact and merely unused, which creates no undefined term.

No double-counting: quantum is argued here under LD and expressly not repeated under the convenience-termination rule, and § 8.13 collection fees / default repricing are correctly treated as pricing mechanics rather than liquidated amounts.
